findings.reason: The protected implementation is already direct, concise, and conventional interview code. Sorting heaters, using bisect_left for the insertion position, comparing only the adjacent left and right heater distances, and retaining the largest local minimum express the complete algorithm without unnecessary abstraction, obscure tricks, or naming defects, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 475, its Python two-array method, and its runnable solve(houses, heaters) adapter. The implementation assigns one common nonnegative radius to all heaters, covers each house through its nearest heater, and returns the smallest radius that covers every house. The nonempty-heater source constraint guarantees every computed local distance is finite.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2064982533 are algorithmically identical: both sort heaters in place, locate each house with bisect_left, compute the same guarded adjacent distances, update the maximum nearest distance, and convert the finite result to int. Their only differences are the native class wrapper and type syntax.

The legal 31-position, 127-position, and 511-position interleaved workloads span more than 16x in both house and heater counts and force nearest-neighbor work throughout each input. The exact current source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.01x the calibrated reference runtime. A correct all-pairs heater scan passed every opaque output but failed only performance at 157.89x the reference runtime.

With h houses and t heaters, the implementation performs O(t log t) sorting and h binary searches of O(log t), which is within the manifest's O((h + t) log(h + t)) time bound. Python's in-place sorting may require O(t) auxiliary storage, while each binary search and distance comparison uses constant additional state.

The current-targeted Approach exactly derives the answer as the maximum nearest-heater distance, explains why only the insertion-position heater and predecessor can be nearest, proves necessity and sufficiency of that maximum, and explicitly defines h and t for its time and space analysis. Its endpoint, duplicate-coordinate, and single-heater cases match the implementation.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the winter heater-standard scenario, horizontal-line positions, identical radius for every heater, minimum-covering-radius objective, all three examples in order, explanation presence for Examples 1 and 2 and absence for Example 3, both constraints, and the absence of visuals, tables, follow-ups, or other source sections.
